senses.def: to go in front of someone or take them somewhere to show the way
examples: The guide led us through the old part of the city.
This path leads to the beach.

senses.def: to be in charge of a group, organization or activity
examples: She was chosen to lead the research team.
Who will lead the party into the next election?

senses.def: to cause something to happen as a result
examples: Too much stress can lead to serious health problems.

senses.def: a position ahead of others in a competition, or a piece of information that helps solve something
examples: Our team took the lead in the second half.
Police are following up several new leads.

note: Irregular: lead – led – led. The metal "lead" (kurşun) is pronounced /led/.

senses.def: a person who is in charge of a group, organization or country
examples: World leaders met in Geneva to discuss climate change.
She's a natural leader who inspires her team.

senses.def: a person, team or company that is ahead of others or the most successful
examples: The company is a world leader in solar technology.

senses.def: the position of being a leader, or the ability to lead people well
examples: Under her leadership, the company doubled its profits.
The job requires strong leadership skills.

senses.def: the people who lead an organization or group
examples: The party leadership refused to comment on the scandal.

senses.def: most important, successful or influential
examples: She is one of the country's leading experts on cancer.
Heart disease is the leading cause of death in the US.

senses.def: having the main part in a play or movie
examples: He played the leading role in the school musical.

note: A "leading question" is one asked in a way that pushes someone toward a particular answer.

senses.def: one of the flat, usually green parts that grow from a plant's stem or branch
examples: A single yellow leaf fell from the tree.
Add a bay leaf to the soup for extra flavor.

note: Plural: leaves. "Turn over a new leaf" means to start behaving better.

senses.def: a printed sheet of paper or a few pages given out free to advertise or inform
examples: Volunteers handed out leaflets about the election outside the station.
The leaflet explains how to recycle properly.

note: More common in British English. Americans usually say "flyer" or "pamphlet".

senses.def: a group of sports teams that play against each other to find the best
examples: The team finished third in the league last season.
He plays in a local basketball league on weekends.

senses.def: a level of quality or ability
examples: That restaurant is way out of my league — it's far too expensive.

note: "Be in league with" = to work secretly with someone, usually to do something bad.

senses.def: to let liquid or gas escape through a small hole, or to escape in this way
examples: The roof leaks every time it rains.
Gas was leaking from a broken pipe.

senses.def: to give secret information to the public or the media
examples: Someone leaked the report to the press before it was published.

senses.def: a small hole that lets liquid or gas escape, or a secret that is made public
examples: There's a leak in the kitchen faucet.
The government is investigating the leak of classified documents.

senses.def: to bend your body in a direction, or to rest against something for support
examples: She leaned forward to hear what he was saying.
He leaned his bike against the wall.

senses.def: to tend to support or prefer a particular opinion or choice
examples: Most voters in the district lean toward the left.

senses.def: having little fat, or using few resources
examples: Choose lean meat like chicken breast.
The startup runs a lean operation with just five employees.

note: "Lean on someone" = depend on them for support. Past: leaned (American) or leant (British).

senses.def: to jump high or a long way, or move somewhere suddenly and quickly
examples: The dog leaped over the fence and ran into the street.
She leaped out of bed when the alarm went off.

senses.def: a long or high jump, or a sudden large increase or change
examples: Sales took a huge leap after the ad campaign.
Moving abroad was a big leap for her.

note: Past: leaped (common in American) or leapt. "Leap at the chance" = accept eagerly.

senses.def: to gain knowledge or a skill by studying, practicing or being taught
examples: I'm learning to play the guitar.
Kids learn languages faster than adults.

senses.def: to find out about something
examples: We learned about the accident from the local news.
She was shocked to learn that she had been fired.

note: Trap: don't say "learn someone something". Use "teach": She taught me Spanish.

senses.def: the process of gaining knowledge or skills
examples: The app makes language learning fun and easy.
Children with learning difficulties may need extra support.

senses.def: knowledge gained by a lot of study
examples: He was a man of great learning and wisdom.

note: "A steep learning curve" means you have to learn a lot quickly.

senses.def: to the smallest degree
examples: This is the least expensive hotel in town.
The problem appeared when we least expected it.

senses.def: the smallest in amount or degree
examples: The bus is the option that uses the least energy.

senses.def: the smallest amount or number
examples: It's the least I can do after all your help.

note: "At least" = not less than / anyway. "Not in the least" = not at all.

senses.def: material made from animal skin, used to make shoes, bags, jackets, etc.
examples: He bought a black leather jacket in Florence.
The sofa is made of real leather.

senses.def: to go away from a person or place
examples: What time do you leave for work?
She left the party early because she had a headache.

senses.def: to let something stay where it is, or to forget to take it
examples: I left my phone in the taxi.
Leave the door open, please.

senses.def: to stop living with someone or stop being part of a job or organization
examples: He left his job to start his own business.

senses.def: a period of time when you are allowed to be away from work
examples: She's on maternity leave until March.
He took two weeks of sick leave.

note: Irregular: leave – left – left. "Leave for" shows destination: "leave for Paris" (Paris'e gitmek üzere ayrılmak).

senses.def: a talk given to a group of people to teach them about a subject, especially at a university
examples: The professor gave a lecture on climate science.
I missed the morning lecture because I overslept.

senses.def: a long, serious talk criticizing someone or telling them how to behave
examples: My dad gave me a lecture about coming home late.

senses.def: to give a talk to teach people, or to criticize someone in a long, serious way
examples: She lectures in economics at a state university.
Stop lecturing me — I know I made a mistake.

note: Trap: Turkish "lektör" is not a lecturer. A "lecturer" is a university teacher (öğretim görevlisi).

senses.def: on the side of your body that is toward the west when you face north
examples: She wears her watch on her left wrist.
The bathroom is the second door on the left side.

senses.def: toward the left side
examples: Turn left at the next traffic light.

senses.def: the left side or direction, or political groups that support social equality and change
examples: The school is on your left after the bridge.
Many on the left criticized the new tax plan.

note: "Left" is also the past of "leave": I left early. "Left over" = remaining.

senses.def: one of the long parts of the body that connect the feet to the rest of the body
examples: He broke his leg playing soccer.
My legs were sore after the long hike.

senses.def: one of the parts that support a table, chair, etc.
examples: One leg of the table is shorter than the others.

senses.def: one part of a journey, race or competition
examples: The band starts the European leg of its tour next month.

note: "Pull someone's leg" = joke with them. "Break a leg!" = good luck (to performers).

senses.def: money or property left to someone after a person's death
examples: She left a large legacy to the local hospital.

senses.def: something, good or bad, that exists as a result of past events or a person's actions
examples: The president's legacy will be judged by future generations.
Pollution is the legacy of decades of heavy industry.

note: In tech, "legacy" describes old systems still in use: legacy software.

senses.def: connected with the law
examples: You should get legal advice before you sign anything.
The company is facing legal action from former employees.

senses.def: allowed by the law
examples: Is it legal to drive with headphones on?
The legal drinking age in the US is 21.

senses.def: an old story about people and events that may or may not be true
examples: According to legend, the lake was formed by a giant's tears.
The legend of King Arthur has been told for centuries.

senses.def: a very famous person, admired for their skill in a particular area
examples: He's a basketball legend who inspired a generation of players.

note: An "urban legend" is a modern story that many people believe but is probably false.

senses.def: very famous and much talked about, often because of special skill
examples: The chef is legendary for his perfect steaks.
The band's legendary 1985 concert is still talked about today.

senses.def: mentioned in old stories
examples: The dragon is a legendary creature found in many cultures.

senses.def: to make a law that affects or controls something
examples: Congress has been slow to legislate on artificial intelligence.
Several states have legislated against smoking in public places.

note: Formal. You can't "legislate morality" means laws cannot force people to be good.

senses.def: a law or set of laws passed by a parliament or government
examples: New legislation will ban single-use plastic bags.
The Senate passed the legislation by a narrow margin.

note: Uncountable: "a piece of legislation", not "a legislation".

senses.def: connected with making and passing laws
examples: Congress is the legislative branch of the US government.
The bill faced several legislative hurdles.

note: The three branches of US government: legislative, executive and judicial (yasama, yürütme, yargı).

senses.def: a group of people with the power to make and change laws
examples: The state legislature voted to raise the minimum wage.
The bill now goes to the legislature for approval.

note: Legislature = the body (meclis); legislation = the laws it makes (mevzuat); legislator = a member (milletvekili).

senses.def: having a fair and acceptable reason
examples: That's a perfectly legitimate question.
Customers have a legitimate reason to complain about the delays.

senses.def: allowed and recognized by law or by accepted rules
examples: Is this a legitimate business or a scam?
The election was seen as free and legitimate.

note: Informal short form: "legit" (That place is totally legit).

senses.def: time when you are not working or studying and can relax
examples: Most people spend their leisure time watching TV or online.
The hotel has excellent leisure facilities, including a pool and spa.

note: "At your leisure" = when it is convenient for you. American pronunciation: /ˈliːʒər/ (LEE-zher).

senses.def: a yellow fruit with sour juice, used in cooking and drinks
examples: Squeeze some lemon over the fish before serving.
She drinks hot water with lemon every morning.

senses.tr: (araba vb.) sürekli arıza çıkaran, çürük mal
senses.def: a product, especially a car, that has many faults (informal, American)
examples: The used car turned out to be a total lemon.

note: In the US, "lemonade" is usually a still drink of lemon juice, sugar and water, not a fizzy soda.

senses.def: to give something to someone for a time, expecting them to give it back
examples: Could you lend me twenty dollars until Friday?
The bank refused to lend them money for a new house.

senses.def: to add a particular quality to something, or to give help or support
examples: The candles lend a romantic feel to the room.
Can you lend me a hand with these boxes?

note: Irregular: lend – lent – lent. Lend = give temporarily; borrow = take temporarily. Turkish "ödünç almak" = borrow.

senses.def: the size of something from one end to the other
examples: The bridge is about two miles in length.
Measure the length and width of the room.

senses.def: the amount of time something lasts or the amount of writing in something
examples: The length of the movie is almost three hours.
Essays should be around 2,000 words in length.

note: "Go to great lengths" = make a big effort. "At length" = for a long time / in detail.

senses.def: very long in time or size, often too long
examples: After a lengthy discussion, they finally agreed on a plan.
The application process is lengthy and complicated.

note: Often slightly negative, suggesting something is longer than necessary.

senses.def: a curved piece of glass or plastic that makes things look larger, smaller or clearer
examples: She bought a new lens for her camera.
I wear contact lenses instead of glasses.

senses.def: a particular way of looking at or understanding something
examples: The book examines history through the lens of women's experience.

note: Plural: lenses. In Turkish "lens" usually means contact lens; in English it means any lens.

senses.def: used about a woman who is sexually attracted to other women, or connected with such women
examples: The film tells the story of a lesbian couple raising two kids.
She was one of the first openly lesbian politicians in the state.

senses.def: a woman who is sexually attracted to other women
examples: The group offers support for lesbians and gay men.

senses.def: to a smaller degree; not so much
examples: The second movie was less exciting than the first.
I've been eating less since I started the diet.

senses.def: a smaller amount of (used with uncountable nouns)
examples: You should spend less time on your phone.
The new model uses less fuel.

senses.def: a smaller amount
examples: The repair cost less than we expected.

note: Traditionally, use "less" with uncountable nouns (less money) and "fewer" with plurals (fewer people).

senses.tr: daha az, daha küçük, daha önemsiz
senses.def: not as great in size, amount or importance as something else
examples: He chose the lesser of two evils and voted for the moderate candidate.
The storm hit the coast hard and inland areas to a lesser extent.

note: Used before nouns or in fixed phrases, never with "than": say "less than", not "lesser than".

senses.def: a period of time when someone is taught something
examples: She takes piano lessons twice a week.
Today's lesson is about the American Civil War.

senses.def: an experience that teaches you something, especially what not to do
examples: Losing all my files taught me a lesson: always make backups.
The government must learn the lessons of the last crisis.

note: Turkish "ders" can also mean a school subject; for that, English says "subject": My favorite subject is math.

senses.def: to allow someone to do something or something to happen
examples: My parents never let me stay out after ten.
Don't let the dog sleep on the bed.

senses.def: used in "let's" to make a suggestion or in "let me" to offer something
examples: Let's grab lunch after the meeting.
Let me help you with those bags.

senses.def: to allow someone to use a room or building in return for rent (mainly British)
examples: They let the apartment to students during the school year.

note: Irregular: let – let – let. No "to" after let: "let me go", not "let me to go". "Let alone" = still less.

senses.def: causing or able to cause death
examples: The drug can be lethal if mixed with alcohol.
He was executed by lethal injection.

senses.def: very harmful or effective (informal)
examples: The striker is lethal in front of the goal.

note: Lethal = able to kill; fatal = actually caused death (a fatal accident).

senses.def: a written message that is sent to someone in an envelope or by email
examples: I received a letter from the bank about my account.
She wrote a cover letter to go with her application.

senses.def: a written symbol that represents a sound in a language
examples: The English alphabet has 26 letters.
Write your name in capital letters.

note: "Follow instructions to the letter" = exactly. A "cover letter" is "ön yazı" for a job application.

senses.def: the amount, degree or standard of something
examples: Pollution levels in the city have risen sharply.
This course is designed for students at an advanced level.

senses.def: the height of something, or a floor in a building
examples: The town is 2,000 feet above sea level.
The parking garage has four levels.

senses.def: having a flat surface that does not slope, or at the same height or position
examples: Make sure the shelf is level before you screw it in.

senses.def: to make something flat, or to destroy a building completely
examples: The earthquake leveled half the town.

note: "A level playing field" = a fair situation for everyone. American spelling: leveled, leveling.

senses.def: an extra amount of money that must be paid, such as a tax
examples: The city introduced a levy on plastic bags.
Airlines pay a levy on every ticket sold.

senses.def: to officially demand and collect a tax or fine
examples: The government plans to levy a new tax on sugary drinks.
A fine was levied on the company for polluting the river.

note: Formal. The verb is usually used with "tax", "fine" or "charge" as object: levy a tax on something.

senses.def: legally responsible for paying for something or for damage
examples: The landlord was held liable for the tenant's injuries.
You may be liable for any damage to the rental car.

senses.def: likely to do something or be affected by something, usually something bad
examples: Old bridges are liable to collapse in strong earthquakes.

note: "Be liable to" is often used for negative possibilities. "Liability" also means a person or thing that causes problems.

senses.def: respecting others' opinions and behavior and supporting personal freedom
examples: She grew up in a liberal household where everything could be discussed.
The city is known for its liberal attitudes.

senses.def: in US politics, supporting social change and government action to help people
examples: Liberal voters strongly supported the healthcare bill.

senses.def: a person who has liberal views
examples: He describes himself as a lifelong liberal.

note: In the US, "liberal" means left-leaning. In Europe and Turkey it often means pro-free-market. "Liberal arts" = humanities.

senses.def: the act of freeing a country, group or person from someone else's control
examples: The city celebrates its liberation from occupation every year.
The women's liberation movement grew rapidly in the 1970s.

senses.def: freedom to live as you choose without too many limits from authority
examples: The constitution protects basic civil liberties.
They fought for liberty and independence.

senses.def: the freedom or right to do something
examples: I'm not at liberty to discuss the details of the case.

note: "Take the liberty of doing" = do something without asking permission. "Take liberties" = act too freely.

senses.def: a building or room where books and other materials are kept for people to read or borrow
examples: I borrowed three novels from the public library.
She spends most afternoons studying in the university library.

senses.def: a collection of books, music, films or software
examples: The app gives you access to a huge music library.

note: Trap: "library" is not "kitapçı" (bookstore). You borrow from a library and buy from a bookstore.

senses.def: an official document that shows you have permission to do, own or use something
examples: You need a valid driver's license to rent a car.
The bar lost its liquor license after the incident.

senses.def: to officially give someone permission to do, own or use something
examples: The restaurant is licensed to serve alcohol.
The software is licensed to schools for free.

note: American English uses "license" for both noun and verb. British uses "licence" (noun) and "license" (verb).

senses.def: to be or put yourself in a flat position, for example on a bed
examples: I just want to lie on the couch and watch TV.
He was lying on the beach reading a book.

senses.def: to be in a particular place or state
examples: The town lies at the foot of the mountains.
The problem lies in poor communication.

senses.def: to say something that you know is not true
examples: He lied about his age to get the job.
Don't lie to me — I know what happened.

senses.def: a statement that you know is not true
examples: She told a lie to avoid getting in trouble.

note: Two verbs: lie – lay – lain (be flat) and lie – lied – lied (say false things). -ing form: lying.

senses.def: the state of being alive, or the period between birth and death
examples: The firefighter risked his life to save the children.
She spent her whole life in the same small town.

senses.def: the way a person lives or a particular part of someone's experience
examples: City life can be stressful.
He keeps his private life out of the media.

senses.def: living things in general
examples: Scientists are searching for signs of life on Mars.

note: Plural: lives /laɪvz/. "For life" = for the rest of your life (a life sentence).
